summary: A ranked lobby 3v2 on Project SD-129, a land ring round a central sea with 9,000-12,000 elmo walks: our three seats in the east (t2 Cortex, t3 and t4 Armada; Opus 5.5 medium players under an Opus 5.5 high commander, Jev 1.14.0) against thebluegecko (Cortex, north) and u6bkep (Armada vehicles, south). The commander's 0:01 plan sprinted t3 to tier 2 on a clock (advanced plant placed 4:00, standing 5:50 on 3,150 metal of standing transfers while t2's and t4's plants paused) and sent every seat's first soldiers into his half to stay, where they died by 6:46; meanwhile thebluegecko's Rascals took t3's undefended spots at 4:21-4:54, u6bkep's Blitzes stood at E6 from 5:02, and from 7:00 his mass stood in our half every minute to the end. After the plant stood the commander put mohos before the army: four advanced constructors before the first Bull at 9:28, 11 mohos at 7,700 energy each with every seat's energy at zero and banks of 1,400-2,650 unspent, while u6bkep's 8 Blitzes and 3 Stouts took t4's home 8:17-9:37 with t2's army held at home and the commander asleep on its 120 s timer. The people's tier-1 vehicles (about 12,000 metal seen by unique id: 41 Brutes, 40 Blitzes, 28 Stouts, 8 Janus) then took the side from 41 extractors at 10:00 to 9 at 14:00 while our two bodies stood at G4/G5, never in his half. All four sessions stopped on the five-hour rate limit at 13:48-14:11, and t3's Bulls and base died to Brutes at 14:14-14:55.

bears_on.id: The tier-2 sprint: trigger, conduct, feeding, the team procedure, tier 1 against tier 2 and 3
bears_on.note: First test of the team procedure against people (a design test episode, E-sd129-2v3). Conduct worked: plant standing in 1:50 on 3,150 metal of standing transfers. But 'with allies beside you the gap is covered' failed here: a 3v2 on a large map with paused feeders and raiders sent away was not covered, and the clock trigger ignored the brief's 'first bank or spots taken'.
'one constructor and then tanks': our advanced plant made four constructors before its first Bull (9:28), and the side's army stayed below what was raiding it. Infern8 is a less experienced player.

A scope limit: the first handful crossed at 2:00-4:20 in a 3v2 with 9,000-12,000 walks and died to his post, armed extractors and Rascals (about 1,900 for 800), leaving nothing at home. The lesson was given for duels whose first soldiers killed nothing.
Reversed: here the people raided our naked outer extractors (t3's four at 4:21-4:54, 49 side-wide), and our answer was one Blitz or none.
The side took the spots (41 at 10:00) but did not hold them: 41 to 9 by 14:00 under tier-1 raids. Holding needs the army where the spots are.

The extractor collapse (10:00-14:00) came minutes before the end; the loss was on extractors and buildings (16,732 lost) not on the army trade (5,736 of soldiers lost against 9,759 of his destroyed, per the commander's traded line in the ledger).
t3 built four converters at 8:25-9:36 on 'metal-bound, not energy' and they drained 280 e/s from the mohos until 11:29.
'less groups': t2's and t3's bodies never fought together; the Bulls split into four groups by ladder hunts at 13:00-13:20; the people's parties were met one at a time.

The brief's team procedure idles the feeders' plants (t4 87 s, t2 51 s) exactly when his raids arrived; t4's plant then stood dead 9:22-11:00 with a full store. The lesson and the procedure pull opposite ways.

What we built told them what was safe: a side of constructors and mohos with few soldiers met 41 Brutes, 40 Blitzes and 28 Stouts and no tier 2 from them. His own word was that Brutes 'apply more pressure'.
'too many construction bots, made and kept out on the map': side builders 24-29 from 8:00 against 30-36 soldiers (team_read).

lens.caveats: No truth file (a lobby game): his numbers are floors from shared sight, and minutes.py's WINDOWS compare our army with what was seen, never a lead. The per-match tools read record-0/strategist-0/jev-0 only, so each seat was read through scratchpad directories of symlinks (seatN with record-N as record-0); analyze_match's 'opponent None' and floor's empty result/minutes follow from no result file. pro_baseline.py not run (Comet only; no SD-129 cards). impedance_sweep counts one session replacement for t3 and t4 that bot.log does not show. No person's reading exists: no computer_whisperer lines in the chat, the ledger row and review.md are model readings, and the main session's memory says the user's reading is pending. Where I differ from the existing review: (a) I add the commander's timer-only wake as a defect behind t4's home (the pleas of 7:43-9:08 reached it at 9:31); (b) t2 did order its army at F6 at 8:59, but the hands never played the attack (fight_to spot_74, then walk to spot_77, apparently under the order's own 'outweighs' clause) and the player reverted at 9:16; (c) I put the sprint's clock trigger against the brief's own trigger; (d) a new open defect, the allies line's income a thousandfold. Otherwise I build on its findings and numbers.

open_questions: Was the sprint wrong for this scenario, or only its cover? The brief says 'long, covered, none: the sprint starts now'; this game was long and 3v2, and the user's reading is pending.

Would t2's eleven Incisors with t4's six soldiers, commander and two Sentries have held t4's home against 8 Blitzes and 3 Stouts at 8:20? The hands walked group_L_t2 to spot_77 at 9:11 instead, apparently judging the party the heavier.
Should a seat's plea, or a seat's plant under fire, wake the commander? At this build only its timer or a person's chat did.
What was his economy? No truth file, and his extractors went unseen from about 9:30.
Has the allies line's thousandfold income figure misled a commander or player in another team game since H-REPORT-ALLIES-LINE was built?
